title: BNCI 2025-002 Continuous 2D Trajectory Decoding dataset
description: EEG recordings from 10 able-bodied participants, plus a feasibility recording from one participant with spinal cord injury, performing attempted lower-arm movements to control a continuous 2D cursor trajectory. Each of the able-bodied participants completed three sessions comprising offline calibration and online feedback with 50% and 100% EEG control. The dataset supports regression-based trajectory decoding, learning effects across sessions, and source-localization analyses for brain-computer interface research.
methods_description: 60-channel EEG (actiCAP, Brain Products) plus 4 EOG channels were recorded at 200 Hz with a right mastoid reference and Fpz ground, with online anti-aliasing (25 Hz) and 50 Hz notch filters. Participants tracked a moving snake target (snakeruns), traced shapes at their own pace (freeruns), or followed targets with gaze only (eyeruns), while attempting mouse-like movements with the strapped lower arm. Preprocessing included downsampling to 100 Hz, bad channel interpolation, eye-artifact subtraction (SGEYESUB), high-pass filtering at 0.18 Hz, common average referencing, HEAR artifact attenuation, low-pass filtering at 3 Hz, and downsampling to 20 Hz. Decoding used PLS regression with UKF smoothing.
